clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country and purchase of the orchard in March 1952, within the year: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, distance between June and Walter as he worked long hours, Glen's fights at school, June keeping to her bed for weeks that winter, Walter's cutoff from his brother Harlan over their father's land money, rows between Walter and June over money for new trees, and June joining the church choir with her anxiety easing and functioning rising by September 1953. The shifts pile up through the first winter and spring in the valley, settling as June found her footing in the community.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter's heavy drinking that summer, conflict between Walter and Glen as they blamed each other for the loan, Glen and Marian taking over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma attacks worsening that winter, Nora beginning to wet the bed in April 1969, Ida's heart trouble found in May 1969, and Walter stopping his drinking and taking work pruning trees by October 1969. The family's shifts pile up through the autumn and winter following the loss, with Walter's functioning rising as the period settles.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's loss of his job in February 1975 when the Ridgeport cannery closed: Glen out of work most of the year and sitting in the truck for hours, loud fights between Glen and Marian over money, Marian taking a second job cleaning offices at night, Nora stopping eating properly and losing weight that summer, Nora keeping to her room and distancing from Marian, Walter drinking again after six years sober, and Nora eating again and making the track team by June 1976 as the period settles. The shifts reach across the family over more than a year, with Nora's functioning rising as things settled.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Hollis's mother Wilma selling her farm and moving into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990: Nora and Wilma clashing over the children's bedtimes and meals, Hollis working late and keeping out of the kitchen rows, Hollis taking his mother's side, Owen having tantrums at preschool, Wilma taking over Lily's care, Nora's eczema flaring on both hands, rows between Nora and Hollis most nights, and Wilma taking a flat in town by June 1991, after which Nora's eczema cleared over the summer. The shifts pile up through the spring and into the winter as the three adults sorted out their places in the household, settling as Wilma moved out.
